name: Real Madrid 2016-18 (Zidane)
scopeNote: Real Madrid under Zinedine Zidane's first spell: appointed 4 Jan 2016 (first match 9 Jan 2016, 5-0 v Deportivo; FourFourTwo/Spielverlagerung first-game pieces dated 10-11 Jan 2016), last match the 2018 Champions League final v Liverpool on 26 May 2018 (Gulf News 23 May 2018 calls it 'Saturday'; the date of the final and of his resignation on 31 May are from general knowledge and not verified in a mined page). Three Champions Leagues (2016, 2017, 2018) and La Liga 2016/17. Rafa Benitez's matches before 4 Jan 2016 are NOT part of this profile. Style: the sources call it a 4-3-3 with the BBC and Casemiro-Kroos-Modric (2016, 2016/17), which Zidane turned into a '4-4-2 diamond' / four-diamond-two with Isco as number 10 (Coaches' Voice) from 2017 (Cardiff) and, in 2017/18, rotated between diamond, flat 4-4-2 and 4-3-3 'sin aparente predilección' (Goal). Tactical writers repeatedly note the lack of a single identity (World Football Index); the popular label 'man-management only' is contested by Sportskeeda and Goal. Counter-pressing collapse in 2017/18 rests on one tier-C source (World Football Index, Jan 2018). Squad age and set-pieces: little evidence found. Not reused from other Real Madrid team files.
openQuestions: Counter-pressing decline in 2017/18 is supported only by World Football Index (tier C, Jan 2018) and Coaches' Voice retrospective on the switch back to 4-3-3; a tier A-B data source (Opta/StatsBomb PPDA) is still missing.
Primary dated source for Zidane quotes not found: all stated-view entries are 'attributed' (press agencies/ESPN FC). The 'innegociable' 4-3-3 quote is only paraphrased by Goal.

Player-empowerment evidence is thin: Ronaldo said he worked 'independently' under Benitez and 'more empathy' with Zidane (Spielverlagerung, Jan 2016); Ronaldo/Bale/Benzema 'not untouchable' (theScore 2016); Ramos 'no egos' (Gulf News 2018). Not enough to show tactical freedom for stars beyond free positional interchange (SI Jan 2016, Spielverlagerung).
Dates of first match (9 Jan 2016) and final (26 May 2018) are not stated in the mined text; confirm from a match database.

Sources disagree on Casemiro: Spielverlagerung 2016 (zonal with man-orientations, Casemiro third midfielder) v 2017 Clasico (pure man-marking, Casemiro v Messi): scheme depended on the opponent, not a stable doctrine.
The Real Champs (2017) says Real defended in a low block and relied on crosses; Spielverlagerung (April 2016) says Madrid pressed high in the Clasico. Phase and opponent dependent.
